correctness.rationale: The original edges are retained. To dominate the new vertex on each edge, the original selected set S must be a vertex cover. Every original vertex outside S then has a selected original neighbor because the base has no isolates. Within S only vertices isolated in G[S] still need selected new neighbors, and their incident edge sets are disjoint, giving precisely the independent nonempty-subset factors and the free factors of the product. In a biclique a cover contains a whole shore. If it also contains vertices of the other shore, all new vertices are redundant; minimality requires exactly one opposite vertex. If the cover is just one shore, exactly one chosen incident new vertex per shore vertex is necessary and sufficient for new-vertex minimality. In each of the four cases every original vertex is also essential, either for the cover condition or to dominate the selected shore. Single-vertex deletion suffices to test minimality by monotonicity. Both-shore covers occur twice only in the full polynomial, where the stated subtraction removes the duplicate. The minimum, maximum and counts follow from the four terms, including tied exponents. For a=2,b≥5 the four exponents are distinct; deleting new vertices first and then the vertices of the size-b shore proves 2-degeneracy. The largest-set fraction has the claimed limit since the competing terms are only quadratic or smaller in b.
residual_risks: The supplied script was not executed. The reported finite enumerations are corroboration, not the basis for the arbitrary-base formula or the biclique classification.

value.rationale: The natural edge-triangulation operator admits a weighted count at every cardinality, not only a minimum-size reduction. In a natural connected 2-degenerate family the separate minimal census shows arbitrarily long gaps and concentration on the largest size while the minimum remains 3. This is explicit structural information about the distribution of minimal open-neighborhood covers, not a tiny isolated computation.
residual_risks: The weighted product still sums over vertex covers and supplies no general efficient algorithm. The four-class census is for bicliques with both shores of size at least two.
